question.text: This corrupt New York political machine supported many Democratic politicians during the late-19th and early-20th centuries. It was depicted as a ferocious tiger by political cartoonist Thomas Nast.
question.clue: This organization was founded by William Mooney and had leaders called "sachems".

swap.leadin: This woman was convicted in 1872 for illegally voting, but refused to pay the fine.
swap.text: Name this champion of women's suffrage who was featured on the 1979 one dollar coin.
swap.clue: This woman is the alleged author of "Marriage and Maternity," an article published in The Revolution.

question.text: After working with steamboats, Vanderbilt rose to the top of the industry making networks of these tracks across the nation. A major event in that industry's history was the construction of a Transcontinental one.
question.clue: In 1906, Congress introduced the Hepburn Act in order to allow maximum rates to be set by a regulator of this industry, the Interstate Commerce Commission.

swap.leadin: Give the following about Native Americans in the United States.
swap.text: This law attempted to eliminate the Native American "communal" way of living by dividing tribal land into allotments of 160 acres for families and 80 acres for individuals.
swap.clue: This 1887 act allowed the U.S. government to survey Indian tribal lands and divide them up among the individuals in the tribe to assimilate Indians into American society.

question.text: This man, whose flagship was the Olympia, led American forces to victory at Manila Bay. He is the only person to have attained the title of Admiral of the Navy.
question.clue: This man annihilated the fleet of Patricio Montojo y Pasaron by issuing the order "You may fire when you are ready, Gridley" while on board his flagship, the USS Olympia.

swap.leadin: Grant attributed his presidential victory to "the sword of Sheridan and the pencil" of this man.
swap.text: Name this editorial cartoonist whose drawings and caricatures led to the downfall of Tammany Hall.
swap.clue: Abraham Lincoln called this man "our best recruiting sergeant."

question.leadin: The Johnstown Flood occurred following the failure of the South Fork Dam owned by this founder of the South Fork Fishing and Hunting Club.
question.text: Name this partner of Andrew Carnegie who locked out members of the Amalgamated Association of Iron and Steel Workers from the Homestead Steel Works.
question.clue: Joseph Duveen advised this man on purchasing works like Vermeer's Officer and Laughing Girl for his Fifth Avenue mansion.

swap.text: William Jennings Bryan gave this speech in support of bimetallism at the 1896 Democratic National Convention. In the final sentences of this speech, he stated, "You shall press down upon the brow of labor this crownof thorns!"
swap.clue: This speech urged the masses not to "press down upon the brow of labor this crown of thorns" in a condemnation of the gold standard.

question.leadin: This man is best known for an event at Baltimore and Potomac Railroad Station.
question.text: Name this man, who stated "I am a Stalwart of the Stalwarts" after his most famous action.
question.clue: This man accused Dr. William Bliss of medical malpractice at his trial, and he purchased a gun with an ivory handle because it would look good in a museum.

swap.leadin: This man is credited with coining the phrase "splendid little war" for the Spanish-American War.
swap.text: Identify this Secretary of State who secured for the United States land it needed to build the Panama Canal in a treaty he signed with Phillipe Bunau-Varilla.
swap.clue: With John George Nicolay, this man co-wrote a ten-volume biography of Abraham Lincoln based on his experience as the President's personal secretary.

question.leadin: Answer the following about legends of the Wild West.
question.text: The oft-romanticized 1881 gunfight between Wyatt Earp's posse and a group of villainous cowboys is usually named for this building in Tombstone, even though the fight actually took place in a lot adjacent to it.
question.clue: The gunfight at this American location only was about 30 seconds and was between the Cochise County Cowboys and a group of officers that included Doc Holliday.

swap.leadin: Seven policemen and four attendees were killed at this event after a pipe bomb was thrown at officers.
swap.text: This important event in labor history took place at a rally held at this site in Chicago.
swap.clue: Illinois Governor John Peter Altgeld pardoned three men implicated in this 1886 bombing and riot, which occurred during a protest against police actions in the McCormick strike.

question.leadin: Name some guys who have served as governor of New York in the 19th century.
question.text: This Governor of New York also served as Secretary of State and helped resolve the dispute over the Alabama Claims, along with helping his President attempt to annex the Dominican Republic.
question.clue: This name was held by a cabinet official who organized a plan to annex the Dominican Republic that was torpedoed by Charles Sumner.

swap.leadin: This term was used by journalists to criticize gilded-age businessmen and their exploitative practices.
swap.text: Give this term that referred to ultra-wealthy industrialists such as John D. Rockefeller.
swap.clue: What derogatory two-word term was used to describe super-rich business leaders in the US in the Gilded Age?

question.text: This outlaw with a brother Frank got his start with Bloody Bill. This notorious bank robber was later assassinated by Robert Ford.
question.clue: His infamy began on February 13, 1866, but a disastrous 1876 incident in Minnesota ended with three of his assistants dead.

swap.text: Cleveland won his first presidency in 1884 after these amusingly named anti-corruption Republicans rejected James G. Blaine in favor of him; they did so despite Blaine's support of the reformist Half-Breeds against the Stalwarts.
swap.clue: Dorman Eaton was another member of this group, which had been alienated by the scandal involving the Little Rock and Fort Smith Railroads, and was denounced in a tirade by the Reverend Samuel Burchard.

question.text: The senate impeached this Secretary of War under Grant for taking kickbacks in an arms deal with France. He resigned before he could be convicted.
question.clue: This Secretary of War under Grant was forced to resign after receiving bribes for post tradership positions. He's the only cabinet secretary to ever have been impeached.

swap.leadin: This man staged A. J. Conway's dramatization of Uncle Tom's Cabin, which created the character Penetrate Partyside and added a happy ending.
swap.text: Name this pro-temperance lecturer who, in the 1870s, served as mayor of Bridgeport, Connecticut, the site of his estate "Iranistan."
swap.clue: He turned a collection of articles he wrote for the New York Weekly Mercury debunking frauds in history into the book Humbugs of the World and went on a European Tour with "General Tom Thumb."

question.leadin: Answer the following about slave narratives.
question.text: Beginning with the author's birth on a Franklin County, Virginia, plantation, this work continues through to his work at Tuskegee. As the name implies, this account emphasizes Booker T. Washington's belief that blacks rise above the past.

swap.leadin: Theodore Roosevelt called this movement "the most American thing in America."
swap.text: Name this adult education movement which mostly featured lecturers giving reform talks or inspirational speeches. It takes its name from the New York lake where the first of these meetings was organized.
swap.clue: Russell Conwell and Maud Ballington Booth were two speakers associated with this adult education movement named for the New York location where it was founded.
